payload.name: PreserveDistinctEventsOnUpdate
payload.description: When a later message describes an activity or plan that could conflict with an existing memory, use before deciding UPDATE: check whether it is the same event by time and activity; if different, ADD instead of overwriting.
content: Before updating an existing memory, verify the new evidence refers to the same real-world event: compare subject, participants, activity/object, and resolved time. If a later message describes a different activity or a different time than the stored memory, do not overwrite the stored memory; ADD a separate memory for the new event unless the later message explicitly retracts, corrects, or supersedes the earlier fact. Keep a specified dated event intact even when a more general later plan exists.

solves: The failure occurred when a later message about a different plan overwrote an existing memory for an earlier specific event, losing a durable fact. The reusable rule is to compare event identity (time, activity, participants) before any UPDATE; only merge/update when the new evidence explicitly supersedes the same event, otherwise create a separate memory. This applies whenever a construction session receives later statements that might conflict with already stored events, but not when the later message explicitly corrects or retracts the same event.
